scope: Native source-closure fixtures in disposable ARM64 Linux VM, 1 CPU and 2 GiB. Real loopback quorum test uses nine voter processes in three groups; cell, admission and key input are synthetic. Time is fixed at 1000 ms, not a live clock.
results: matching live lease permits synthetic cell and receipt
expired lease and rogue mode refused before cell
changed lease or absent quorum after cell suppresses receipt
clock regression suppresses receipt; bypass mutant signs
real three-voter loopback quorum accepted live lease, refused expired lease, and suppressed receipt after two voters were stopped during a delayed synthetic cell
observation: The initial fault-injection attempt observed the marker only at process exit because native stdout was buffered; the test-only cell now flushes via stderr before delay, and the final run observed its in-flight marker before stopping voters.
limits: Same-VM unauthenticated loopback, synthetic cell/key/admission and fixed clock; no remote Mac, actual bot, authenticated quorum, real clock drift, process-tree control, sink-side effect fencing or governor. Once a cell starts, suppressing a receipt cannot undo or fence its effects. No blind retry of an unconfirmed outcome.
